page: Microsoft Azure M16bds_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by a dedicated 4.0 GHz Intel Xeon 8473C processor featuring 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware instruction extensions include AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and VAES. The configuration is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, alongside a 105 MB L3 cache. Local storage includes a 429 GB SSD, and no GPUs are attached.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent single-threaded execution and balanced multithreaded capacity. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2,196.0, placing it in the top 25 percent, alongside strong single-threaded gzip compression at 32.97 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 13.74 GB/sec. Multithreaded workloads register typical performance for this tier, including a multi-core Geekbench score of 13,388.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 27,937.56. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 107.61 GB/sec with write speeds of 68.03 GB/sec, while in-memory operations deliver 22.55 million Redis SET operations per second.

The hardware design balances large memory capacity per core with included high-speed local disk storage, supporting applications that demand significant memory footprints without paying for excess compute cores. While overall multi-core compute throughput sits in the middle tier, the high single-thread ratings and advanced vector and matrix capabilities offer steady efficiency for memory-bound tasks.

This server type is primarily suited for enterprise in-memory caches, relational database engines, medium-scale data analytics, and general memory-intensive workloads requiring dedicated host resources.
